notes.decision: Chapter-end colophon: a single ⲯⲑ '99' standing alone marks the boundary closure of the previous chapter (chapter 98 on the senses of virgin/continent), before the new chapter heading at line 32 introduces chapter 99 on transmutation.
Chapter heading framed by chapter number on both sides — standard Manichaean Kephalaia chapter-display convention. Chapter 99 'Concerning the Transmutation/Transmigration.'

Translated 'signal at them' preserving the gestural-semantic register of ⲭⲱⲣⲙⲉ ('make a sign, wink, signal,' already in glossary as silent communication). Here in the eschatological register: the cosmic powers signal/beckon souls toward the metarrismos (transformation/repentance). The repeated phrase ⲥⲉⲭⲱⲣⲙⲉ ⲛ̄ⲥⲱⲩ ⲁⲧⲙⲉⲧⲁⲣⲣⲓⲥⲙⲟⲥ (lines 3, 5, 7, 10) is the technical formula of this kephalaion's question.

ⲡⲕⲩⲥ rendered 'the Lord' as a contracted/abbreviated form of κύριος (cf. ⲡⲁⲭⲁⲓ̈ⲥ in glossary as Lyc 'Lord' from ⲡϫⲟⲉⲓⲥ; here written ⲡⲕⲩⲥ may be a Greek-derived abbreviation). ⲁⲩⲭⲑⲟⲥ rendered 'he answered them' tentatively — the form is otherwise unattested in our corpus and may represent a Lycopolitan/scribal variant of ⲁϥⲟⲩⲱϣⲃ̄-ⲟⲩ 'he answered them' or a related speech-act verb. Context (introducing the Apostle's reply to a question) demands a verb of speech-response.

Greek loanword παίδευσις 'training, discipline, education' retained in transliteration to mark its technical force in this kephalaion. Recurs 6 times (lines 16, 17, 18, 19, 21, 22) as the controlling concept: παίδευσις in the world (parents disciplining children) parallels but is not identical with the παίδευσις given to catechumens at metarrismos. Companion verb ⲡⲁⲓⲁⲉⲩⲉ = παιδεύειν 'to train, discipline.'

Translated 'young ones' based on context (children disciplined by parents/teachers paralleling 'sons'). Cf. accumulated glossary entry ⲕⲉⲃⲁⲩⲟⲛⲉ 'commoners/common folk (tentative)' which is the bare lexeme ⲃⲁⲩⲟⲛⲉ + ⲕⲉ- 'other.' Here in disciplinary context with ⲩⲏⲣⲉ 'sons,' the sense is more specifically 'junior/ordinary' children — those of the household receiving training alongside the master's own sons.

Translated 'sword' as Lycopolitan reflex of ⲥⲏϥⲉ (Lyc ⲏⲩⲉ for ⲏϥⲉ — same vowel-semivowel pattern attested in this corpus, e.g. ⲥⲟⲁⲡⲉⲧ for ⲥⲡⲟⲧⲟⲩ). Used metaphorically for the disciplinary instrument applied to children: ⲟⲩⲱⲧ ⲧⲥⲏⲩⲉ ... ⲟⲩⲱⲧ ⲧⲥⲏⲩⲉ 'one is the sword..., one is the sword...' = the same disciplinary tool serves both classes. The 'sword' image fits the parental παίδευσις context (rod-of-discipline) without literal violence.

Rendered 'falls (into error)' tentatively. The verb is a Lycopolitan form whose root is uncertain in this corpus. Possible candidates: ⲡⲱϩⲧ̄ 'fall, cast down' (with ⲩ for ⲡ unusual but possible); ϣⲟⲩϩⲧ̄ 'be cut, fail'; ⲱϣⲧ̄ 'be oppressed, hung.' In the disciplinary context where parents respond to a son's misbehavior, 'falls (into sin/error)' best fits — paralleling ⲣ̄-ⲛⲁⲃⲉ 'sin' of the preceding line.

Translated 'make a marvel/spectacle of him' — the verb ⲣ̄-ⲉⲡⲡⲏⲣⲉ literally 'do a wonder' but in disciplinary context functions as 'make an example of him' (public reproof). The double ⲡ may reflect the form ⲣ̄-(ⲡ)ⲉ-ⲡⲏⲣⲉ 'do the wonder.' Confidence moderate; the gist is clear but the precise nuance awaits parallels.

Translated 'shall be slain' reading ϣⲱⲧϩ as Lycopolitan reflex of ϣⲱⲧⲃ̄ 'kill, slay' (regular ⲍ/ϩ for ⲃ in Lyc.; final -ϩ may reflect dialectal devoicing). Punitive context (lines 3-7 catalogue torments inflicted on sinners — suffering, binding, cutting members) supports a violence-verb. Alternative reading ϣⲱⲧⲡ̄ 'sleep, fall asleep' (= euphemism for dying) is also possible. Confidence moderate.

Read as ϣⲁⲩ-ⲙⲁⲣⲉ̄ 'they habitually bind' (with ⲕ likely a scribal error for ⲩ, given preceding habitual ϣⲁⲩⲍⲣⲓⲥⲉϣ 'they habitually suffer' which establishes the iterative-punitive register). ⲙⲁⲣⲉ from ⲙⲟⲩⲣ 'bind.' Alternative: ϣⲁⲕ- as 2sg habitual ('thou habitually bind') — unlikely in this 3pl context. Confidence low.

Greek loanword παίδευσις 'education, training, instruction.' Lyc. ⲁⲓⲁⲉⲩ for παιδευ- with ⲁⲉⲩ for δευ. Translates as 'education' or 'training/discipline' — fits the catechetical context where the catechumens receive instruction in righteousness. Spans lines 8-10 with article ⲧⲡⲁⲓ-|ⲁⲉⲩⲥⲓⲥ split across line break.

Plural of Greek τύχη 'fortune, fate, allotted lot' with Lyc. plural ending -ⲁⲩⲉ. Standard Greek loanword in cosmological-eschatological register; the catechumens' ⲧⲩⲭⲁⲩⲉ are their assigned fates, paralleling κλήρος in this corpus.

Greek κεράννυμι 'mix, blend' adopted into Coptic as verbal stem ⲕⲉⲣⲁ-. Circumstantial ⲉⲩ- 'while/as they are mingled.' Refers to the eschatological mingling of catechumen souls with their fates/places.

Habitual 3pl on ϩⲣⲁⲕ 'be still, calm' (Lyc ⲍ for ϩ; cf. accumulated ⲧⲍⲣⲕⲟ/ⲍⲣⲁⲕ in glossary). 'They habitually become still' — likely the silenced/resigned state of bound sinners, paralleling line 18's binding.

Lycopolitan teacher-address idiom 'I am declaring to you (pl.)' — already attested in accumulated vocabulary. The construction ⲭⲉ + ⲛⲉⲓ̈ⲉⲧⲧⲏⲛⲉ + vocative (ⲛⲕⲁⲧⲏⲭⲟⲩⲙⲉⲛⲟⲥ 'O catechumens') is the standard Mani-to-disciples discourse-frame.
